messages:
kevin_cs: FYI customer cust_8421 reported sudden credit drain overnight, asked for emergency review. Zendesk #9983. They say a background job hit embeddings + rerank and burned ~450k tokens instead of ~45k. :grimacing:

maria_support: I've attached their billing snapshot in the ticket. Asked for the worker logs and schedule. Offered provisional 10k credits while we investigate. Ticket note: 'Customer running nightly dedupe/embedding job; sees unexpected spike.' :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kevin_cs: Important: they tried to apply a promo code earlier and said it didn't apply, then credits went negative. Might be related but prob separate. Repro priority: high.

alex_eng: @kevin_cs can you paste the example job manifest or the curl call the customer used? Need to reproduce rate/size. Also, please include request IDs from their recorded calls (X-Request-ID or our x-rw-request-id header).

kevin_cs: Pasted from ticket (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer...
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "open-embed-large",
  "inputs": [... batch of 25k short texts ...]
}
```
They also call /v1/rerank in the same job for scoring.

alex_eng: Thanks. Two immediate suspects: 1) their worker had aggressive retries with no idempotency key, causing duplicate requests on transient failures; 2) batching was smaller than expected (lots of small calls -> more per-token overhead).

alex_eng: Quick repro steps for eng:
1) Spin a background job sending 25k items in N batches (simulate splits of 100, 500, 1000).
2) Introduce intermittent 5xx responses (client-side retry policy: 5 retries with no jitter).
3) Observe duplicate calls to embeddings/rerank.

Snippet to simulate (use idempotency header to avoid duplicates):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: <job-run-id>" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large","inputs":[...]}'
```

maria_support: Customer says they did re-run the job a few times after errors, because their queue didn't mark jobs as finished. Could be client-side.

alex_eng: @maria_support can you ask for their worker retry policy and the exact timestamps of the re-runs? We'll correlate with request logs. I can grep by customer_id and by x-rw-request-id if they provide one.

billing-bot: provisional credit 10000 applied to cust_8421 (action: manual_grant by maria_support). Promo code application log: promo "REDWOOD-TRIAL-2024" failed for cust_8421 earlier due to trailing whitespace in code field -> normalized and re-applied, but original failure had no rollback.

kevin_cs: Noted. Customer still upset that credits disappeared before promo landed. Asked for an explanation and rollback of unexpected charges.

alex_eng: Target actions from eng: 
- Check server-side deduplication: do we treat repeated requests with same Idempotency-Key as idempotent for embeddings/rerank? If not, add/confirm.
- Query logs for 1714000400..1714001200 for cust_8421, filter by endpoint (/v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank) and look for repeated request bodies / similar token counts.
- Check our retry handling in ingest path: are we re-submitting to the billing pipeline on client retries?

sre-bot: New alert: rate of embedding requests for customer cust_8421 spiked to 450 rps at 1714000505 -> mitigated by routing policy after 30s.

alex_eng: Suggested mitigations for customer (temporary):
- Disable background worker or pause queue for that customer, then resume with batching tuned to 500 items per request.
- Add Idempotency-Key header per job-run.
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter and max_retries=2 for long jobs.
- Use bulk-embeddings endpoints (if available) that report consumed tokens before final commit.

maria_support: I've communicated temp credit grant and pause suggestion. Customer asked for a full rollback for the night. Can we offer rollback + extra trial credits while we root cause?

alex_eng: I recommend rollback for unexpected duplicate calls that we can correlate from logs (if duplicates > 1 and timestamps within retry window). If duplicates are clearly client-caused (multiple re-queues without idempotency) we should still consider a one-time courtesy rollback + 20k trial credit and work with them on best-practice config.

kevin_cs: Please confirm: who will run the logs query and hand back a list of duplicated request IDs?

alex_eng: I'll run the logs query (ETA 30m). Query I'll use:
```
-- pseudo SQL for internal logs
SELECT request_id, endpoint, body_hash, count(*) as hits, min(timestamp) as first_ts, max(timestamp) as last_ts
FROM api_request_logs
WHERE customer_id='cust_8421'
  AND timestamp BETWEEN 1714000400 AND 1714001200
  AND endpoint IN ('/v1/embeddings','/v1/rerank')
GROUP BY request_id, body_hash
HAVING hits > 1
ORDER BY hits DESC;
```

maria_support: I'll update the ticket with the provisional credit and that eng is investigating. Customer: "please expedite, this is blocking billing reconciliation". :pleading_face:

billing-bot: Note: automatic promo re-apply succeeded at 1714001600. System detected earlier promo failure reason: 'invalid_chars' (trailing space).

kevin_cs: Thanks all. Alex pls post results of that query here and confirm if duplicates exist. If they do, we proceed with rollback and additional trial credits.

alex_eng: Will update in ~30. :eyes:

sre-bot: Reminder: add telemetry tag `bulk_embedding` to any mitigation rollouts so we can track if this pattern repeats for other customers.

kevin_cs: Closing loop: once eng posts duplicated request list, billing will enact rollback and add 20k trial credit. maria_support to confirm to customer.

[thread ends]")
